# Fixed owned C direct-worker CPU lifecycle observations

Two separate fresh N1-1 CPU cases observed one fixed C coordinator/controller/guard/worker product each. The source was reviewed, pushed and integrated through [PR42](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/pull/42) before either host episode. [Exact source documentation](https://github.com/Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev/blob/192119b34347adeb88f0faefe5591d6261c9a0c0/docs/frontier-v8-owned-c-lifecycle.md) states the closed protocol and its limits.

| Case | Returned fixed-role outcome | Worker-directed signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| normal | Coordinator reaped controller176247 and guard176248 with exit0; guard reaped worker176249 with exit0 | None |
| controller_loss | Coordinator reaped controller177002 with exit23 and guard177003 with exit0; guard reaped worker177004 with raw wait status9/SIGKILL | One owned-worker pidfd SIGKILL attempt, result0 |

The normal coordinator PID was176246 and the loss coordinator PID was177001. Returned boot/UID1000/PID-birth/PPID/product and private nonce packets matched the declared fixed roles. Guard binding preceded worker creation; case ARM/ACK preceded the controller command. The normal guard observed controller exit before worker completion. The loss guard rechecked identity/product/deadline after controller exit and before the sole signal, then observed worker exit and performed its parent-only wait. The shared monotonic deadline epoch and terminal-before-guard-reap protocol passed the independent actual audit. These are controlled-source returned facts, not full ancestry or continuous code authentication.

Both cases reported four managed pidfd records with one close and immediate F_GETFD=-1/EBADF9 each, plus the worker's inherited controller-copy close and unused-pipe closures. The inherited-close ledgers contain9 controller,6 guard and5 worker entries per case. Kind plus descriptor number distinguishes legitimate private-pipe reuse of standard-stream numbers; the guard worker pidfd was descriptor1. Coordinator cleanup-signal attempts were zero. Per case, four compiler stages, one link and one runtime returned zero and were normally reaped with no outer kill/timeout. Normal toolchain subprocesses and Python/bootstrap activity are additional to the four C roles.

The actual current system headers supplied symbolic SYS_pidfd_open and SYS_pidfd_send_signal; runtime facts reported their constant values434 and424, with SIGKILL9/POLLIN1/POLLNVAL32/EBADF9 and compiler-matching scalar sizes. Source calls reviewed symbolic header constants and signatures. Those numbers were observed here rather than guessed from an architecture or provider filename. Each dependency inventory contains147 entries including the C translation unit, and each postlink LOAD inventory has13 aliases. The actual ELF PT_INTERP was parsed. Driver/header/link/product/interpreter and input/self/marker/output boundaries were rechecked before and after runtime. Link-file payload snapshots occurred after linking and do not authenticate all bytes throughout the link or complete mapped code.

Normal original returned observer stdout is74,715 bytes, SHA256 `bb975c876050633418e12b054e746dbc941c2deff7d9cc02796345a77dda7624`; loss is75,501 bytes, SHA256 `db5db23a612b4ca83a9cad64027d333f142f21bc7d1e07158b7cc09bec8921ba`. Both stderr streams are empty. Each case used two declared SSH invocations and one SCP invocation; all six invocations returned0 with no local timeout. Underlying socket connections/multiplexing were not measured. The launch transports elapsed1.997313s and2.004914s respectively, including transport and observation; these are not model latency or performance results.

The observer embedded parsed C facts and reported the C stdout artifact size/hash (normal7896 bytes, loss8143 bytes). Those remote C stdout bodies, compiler streams, headers, CPP, objects, products, link map, interpreter, markers and receipt bodies were not independently retrieved or rehashed. A hash plus parsed values cannot reconstruct the exact original C stdout. Returned marker/receipt write and postvalidation facts are not independent remote durability proof. Node alias, physical exclusion, full ancestry, descriptor inode/acquired flags and full mapped code remain unverified.

Only `normal_owned_direct_worker_lifecycle_observed` for the normal case and `controlled_controller_loss_worker_reaped_observed` for the loss case are true. Functional containment, production controller/guard, general descendants, guard/coordinator/observer/host-loss cleanup, execution availability, resource authority, GPU/foreign restoration and model-runtime ABI remain unavailable. The loss case deliberately exits one logical controller while its coordinator and guard survive; it does not observe loss of every controller component. The worker does not exec, create arbitrary descendants or run models. Async interruption or failed terminal writing can leave incomplete evidence or unknown cleanup. Outer backend timeout handles only its direct child. Dynamic negative C cleanup and clock branches remain unproved by portable synthetic fixtures. No Torch/model/tensors/gradients/training/pip check/installation/CUDA initialization/GPU/foreign queue/browser action/external trial occurred.
